newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: SOCCER-PORTUGUESE CHAMPIONS SUFFER SHOCK DEFEAT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PORTUGUESE CHAMPIONS SUFFER SHOCK DEFEAT.

text.p: Portuguese first division champions Porto suffered their first away defeat of the season when they conceded two goals in the second half to lose 2-1 to Braga on Saturday night.
Porto clinched their third successive title two weeks ago and now lead the table with one match remaining on 82 points, followed by Sporting on 69 with a match in hand. Benfica are third with 58.

Porto, missing league top scorer Mario Jardel of Brazil who is recovering from a shoulder operation, opened the scoring in the fourth minute when midfielder Joao Costa curved a 20-metre shot over Braga goalkeeper Rui Correia's head.
In the 47th minute Croat striker Mladen Karoglan levelled the score for fourth-placed Braga with a second attempt after Porto's Swedish 'keeper Lars Eriksson was unable to secure his first shot.
Braga, who had not won at home against Porto for 18 years, scored their winner in the 68th minute when an unmarked Toni Duarte hit home a header from inside the box.
Benfica suffered a similar surprise 2-0 home defeat to Guimaraes on Friday, the latest humiliation in what has been the worst season in the club's history.
Benfica will be looking to salvage some credibility by winning the Portuguese Cup final against Boavista on June 10.
